headline: Issued a favorable report to the Legislative Council on Mill River Trail construction, with one abstention.
summary: Discussed concerns about construction costs for the Mill River Trail, which staff said cannot be known until after design. Approved the August 11, 2026, minutes as written. Heard that a six-month moratorium on data centers may be proposed.
decisions: Recommended a favorable report to the Legislative Council on the Mill River Trail construction referral, with one abstention (Bauer).
Approved the August 11, 2026, meeting minutes as written, with one abstention (Bauer).

October 5, 2026 
The Planning and Zoning Commission, Town of Hamden, held a hybrid Regular Meeting on 
Tuesday, September 22, 2026. The meeting was held in-person in the Legislative Council Chambers 
at Hamden Memorial Town Hall, 2372 Whitney Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518, and remotely via 
Town Zoom teleconferencing at https://www.hamden.zoom.us/j/82468227728.  
 
Commissioners in Attendance: 
 
In Person: Michele Mastropetre (Chairman), Joseph McDonagh 
(Vice Chairman), Barbara Andrews, Richard Bauer, 
Richard Pearce, Hannah Leckman, Felicia Bond, 
Ronald Leonardo, Calvin DeMarsilis 
  Staff in Attendance: In Person: Eugene Livshits (Town Planner), Christopher Soto 
(Assistant Town Planner), Tim Lee (Assistant Town 
Attorney), Maisie Albis (Commission Clerk) 
  
Chairman Mastropetre called the meeting to order at 7:03p.m. The clerk read the agenda into the 
record, and Commissioners and staff introduced themselves.  
 
A. Public Comment Session 
 Chairman Mastropetre called for comments from the public regarding matters within the purview 
of the Commission but not already on the agenda. No in-person or remote attendees made comments.  
Commissioner Bauer asked if the correspondence contained in members’ meeting packets should 
be noted on the record. The clerk reported that a letter had been received on September 16, 2026, 
from Mr. Gary Williams. Chairman Mastropetre reviewed the letter, which regarded the recently 
approved Special Permit #26-1400 at 2693 Whitney Avenue. Mr. Williams raised concerns about the 
applicant being in violation of the approval. Mr. Livshits confirmed to the Chairman that a Zoning 
Enforcement Officer will be looking into the issue.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
B. Regular Meeting 
 1. C.G.S. §8-24 Review #26-451 
Mill River Trail Construction (State Project 061-0159)  
Applicant: Town of Hamden 
Chairman Mastropetre requested that Mr. Soto read his report regarding the application. In it, 
he explained that the referral was requesting authorization for the design work and eventual
Page 2 of 3 Planning and Zoning Commission 9.22.26 Minutes 
 
construction of the proposed Mill River Trail. The report concluded with a recommendation that 
the Commission issue a favorable report to the Legislative Council.  
The Chairman asked Mr. Soto if there was funding in place for maintenance of the trail once it 
has been constructed. He replied that he could not speak directly to what funding the Engineering 
Department might have planned, but noted that the trail would be a standard hardscape of bike 
lanes and sidewalks that would incorporate existing infrastructure. Mr. Livshits later confirmed 
with the Town Engineer that much of the trail would be replacing existing sidewalks rather than 
new installation. 
Commissioner DeMarsilis asked who would own the trail and therefore absorb responsibility 
for liabilities. Mr. Soto did not have that information. He referred members to the packets of 
materials that had been provided as part of the application.  
The Commission discussed the budget figures provided in the packets. There were concerns 
about construction costs, which were seemingly unaddressed. Mr. Livshits explained that those 
costs could not be known until after the design phase. He and Mr. Soto reminded the Commission 
that they were responsible for determining whether the proposal was an appropriate use of the 
land, and that the financial aspects fall under the purview of the Legislative Council.  
Commissioner McDonagh moved to issue a favorable report to the Legislative Council 
regarding the referral. Commissioner Pearce seconded. Chairman Mastropetre called for a 
vote. Commissioner Bauer abstained from voting. All others were in favor of the motion. 
The Commission issued a favorable report regarding C.G.S. §8-24 Referral #26-451.  
 
 C. Old Business 
 
 
 
1. Review of August 11, 2026, Regular Meeting minutes 
 Commissioner McDonagh moved to approve the August 11, 2026, minutes as written. 
Commissioner Leckman seconded. Commissioner Bauer abstained from the vote, as he had 
not been present at the meeting. All others voted in favor; the minutes were approved as 
written. 
   
D. New Business 
 
 
 
 
      
 1. Potential Moratorium on Data Centers 
Mr. Livshits reported that the Planning and Zoning Department may be presenting an 
application for a moratorium on data centers at an upcoming meeting. He said that the proposed 
moratorium would be for a period of six months in order to give the Department time to conduct 
research and draft applicable regulations for the use. Chairman Mastropetre asked whether 
external consultants would be involved. Mr. Livshits replied that the work would begin with 
Department staff but that he would seek additional assistance if necessary.

E. Adjournment  
 Commissioner Bauer moved to adjourn. Commissioner Bond seconded and all were in 
favor. Chairman Mastropetre adjourned the meeting at 7:25 p.m.
